- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is rising.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias in second half of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by > 5% in first 7 days, assume momentum bias; adjust next 7 days downward by 1–3%.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average before output.
